messages:
incident-bot: Pager — KV cache fragmentation + cuda alloc failures in prod (us-west-2). Alerts: kv_fragmentation_pct > 65%, cuda_alloc_fail_rate > 3%. Links: https://infra.alerts/redwood/alerts/1860123456 :rotating_light:

sam: Oncall here, acknowledging. Looking at graphs now.

alex: I'm awake, joining. Which pool/cluster?

sam: pool-gpu-2 (inference-worker). p99 token latency has spiked, increased 502s on chat routes. Started ~14:01 PST.

jia: I'm seeing lots of small allocations and allocation retries. Logs include repeated: \"RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while allocating tensor (requested 8.00 MiB)\" from kv_cache allocator; fragmentation histogram shows many tiny free blocks.

matt: We pushed a batching config change ~2h ago: continuous batching max_batch_tokens bumped from 2048 -> 8192, and we loosened pack-timeouts to help throughput. That may have increased allocator pressure.

alex: Ok first mitigations: 1) disable continuous batching on pool-gpu-2, 2) set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 on worker pods, 3) rolling restart of inference-worker to drop stale cuda caches.

sam: I'll apply config change to disable continuous batching now (patching feature flag via console).

ops-bot: Feature flag update applied: kv_continuous_batching_enabled=false for pool-gpu-2 (:white_check_mark:)

eng-runtime-bot: Triggering rolling restart: kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/inference-worker-pool-gpu-2 ; strategy=rolling, maxUnavailable=1

jia: Pushing env change: adding env var PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 to deployment spec and restarting pods. This forces allocator to prefer splitting large chunks which reduces fragmentation for lots of small allocations.

sam: Also patching runtime config to lower batch_timeout_ms -> 20ms and batch_max_tokens -> 2048 as a fast safety cap.

alex: Good. Commands used: 
```
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/inference-worker-pool-gpu-2 PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/inference-worker-pool-gpu-2
```

matt: Can we also temporarily disable the long-hold cache for kv entries older than 60s? That will free some device memory sooner.

jia: I pushed a canary to reduce kv_cache_ttl from 5m -> 60s on 2 pods. If stable, will roll.

incident-bot: Canary metrics (5 min): cuda_alloc_fail_rate reduced 4.1% -> 1.0% on canary nodes; overall cluster still at 2.8%.

alex: Rolling the config to 100% now. Monitoring p99 and error rate.

eng-runtime-bot: Restart complete. All pods back up. Healthchecks passing.

jia: Quick log snippet from host-12 before restart: 
```
[14:05:12] WARN kv_allocator: fragmentation=72.4%, free_chunks=1423, alloc_retries=9
[14:06:03] ERROR runtime: cudaMalloc returned out-of-memory (function alloc) - retrying
```

sam: Are customers impacted? CS?

matt: Two customers (acct-9923, acct-1145) reported 5-10% of requests failing with 502 between 14:02-14:18 PST. We've notified the CS team; they are drafting outreach.

incident-bot: Cluster metrics update: p99_latency_tokens improved 1.8s -> 0.95s within 6 minutes of restart and env change. Error rate down to 0.4%. :white_check_mark:

jia: There's still elevated fragmentation metrics on GPU0 of host-12 — looks like long-lived alloc patterns left some slab remnants. We'll run targeted compaction on that host to defragment.

alex: Next steps/owner list: 
- jia: run targeted compaction + follow up instrumentation (kv cache per-chunk size distribution).
- matt: customer impact tracker & CS outreach.
- eng-runtime: draft allocator heuristic patch (consider fallback to splitting allocations earlier).
- sam: coordinate postmortem and add runbook entry.

sam: Handoff to alex for follow-up actions (I need to go offline at 15:00 PST).

alex: Taking over. Creating incident ticket INC-2026-342 and setting priority P1. I'll own the postmortem.

incident-bot: Handoff noted — oncall changed to alex.

jia: Running compaction script on host-12 now (limit: 2 nodes at a time). I'll report back with before/after fragmentation histograms.

alex: Thanks team. Closing the active pager for now — reopen if alloc_fail_rate rises above 1% or p99 latency exceeds 1.5s. We'll capture timeline + root cause in a follow-up postmortem. :memo:
summary: Pager for high KV cache fragmentation and CUDA allocation failures in prod. Mitigations: disabled continuous batching, set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128, lowered batch caps, rolling restart of inference workers. Metrics improved; small customer impact recorded; handoff to alex for postmortem and longer-term allocator fixes.
